title: Whole Numbers
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Place value is taught on a chart with the three groups (millions, thousands, ones) labelled, the ones place first. Squares and roots are taught as a square of dots or a square plot before any rule.

skills.key_step: The child names the place by counting from the ones on the right, group by group, and says the group name (millions, thousands) as part of the place.

floor.prerequisite: Knows place value up to hundreds of thousands.
floor.question: In 352,610 which place is the 3 in?

representations: a number written on a place value chart with the three groups labelled
the same number with only commas, read aloud
a real number such as a county population
steps: Write the number on the chart from the ones end.
Say the group each digit is in: millions, thousands or ones.
Inside the group, count ones, tens, hundreds from the right.
Join the two: "ten" + "thousands".
contexts: the population of Nakuru County
a school budget in shillings
the number of voters in a constituency

board.do: Draw a chart with three groups: millions, thousands, ones, each split into hundreds, tens and ones.
Write 4,206,315 into the chart from the ones place.
Point at the 2.
board.say: Which group is the 2 in, and which place inside the group?

board.do: Wait for the child to name the group and the place.
Write "hundred thousands" above the 2.

misconceptions.ask: If the number had one more digit at the front, would the 2 change its place?
misconceptions.repair: Places are counted from the ones end, so the front of the number does not decide them.

misconceptions.ask: What is in the hundred thousands box of 3,050,600?
misconceptions.repair: A zero fills its place; count it like any digit.

listen_for: ten thousands is the first one
misconceptions.ask: Point at the thousands group: which box is ten thousands, counting from its right?
misconceptions.repair: Inside a group the order from the right is ones, tens, hundreds: thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands.

misconceptions.ask: Read the whole number aloud. In which part do you say the 2?
misconceptions.repair: Every place in the middle group carries the word thousand.

checks.question: In 7,083,415 which place is the 8 in?
checks.shows: a zero in the hundred thousands place

checks.question: Which digit is in the hundred thousands place in 2,964,507?

skills.key_step: The child finds the place of the digit first and then says its total value as the digit times that place, with zeros for every place to its right.

floor.prerequisite: Names the place of a digit up to millions.
floor.question: In 4,370,215 which place is the 7 in?

representations: a place value chart with the digit circled
the digit with a zero written in every place to its right
expanded form written under the number
steps: Find the place of the digit.
Write the digit and put a zero in every place to its right.
Read it: 7 ten thousands is 70,000.
For expanded form, do this for every digit that is not zero and add them.
contexts: a cheque for a county project
the cost of a matatu in shillings
the number of tea bushes on an estate

board.do: Write 4,370,215 on the chart.
Circle the 7.
board.say: How many places are to the right of the 7?

board.do: Count the places to the right with the child: one, two, three, four.
Write 7 followed by four zeros under it.
Ask the child to read the total value aloud.

misconceptions.ask: What is the 7 worth in this number?
misconceptions.repair: The total value is a number: the digit times its place, 70,000.

misconceptions.ask: How many places are to the right of the 6?
misconceptions.repair: Write one zero for each place to the right of the digit.

misconceptions.ask: Is 215 part of what the 7 is worth?
misconceptions.repair: Only the digit and zeros: the other digits have their own values.

misconceptions.ask: Add your terms back up. Do you get 3,050,600?
misconceptions.repair: Each term keeps the place of its digit; a zero in the number still counts as a place.

checks.question: What is the total value of 5 in 3,520,146?

skills.key_step: The child puts each spoken part in its own group of three on the chart and fills every empty place with a zero before joining.

floor.prerequisite: Writes numbers up to hundreds of thousands in figures.
floor.question: Write "four hundred and two thousand and fifty" in figures.

representations: three boxes of three places: millions, thousands, ones
the number with commas between the groups
a number read aloud and written down
steps: Draw the three groups.
Put the millions part in the millions group.
Put the thousands part in the thousands group, with zeros so it has three digits.
Do the same for the ones group, then join with commas.
contexts: a news report of a county budget
the number of trees planted in a campaign
shillings raised at a harambee

board.do: Draw three boxes of three places, labelled millions, thousands and ones.
Write "5 million, 40 thousand and 8" above them.
Ask the child to write each part in its box.
board.say: Which box does the 40 go in, and how many digits must that box have?

board.do: Wait for the child to fill the empty places.
Write 5,040,008 and read it aloud.

misconceptions.ask: How many digits must the thousands box have?
misconceptions.repair: Every group after the millions has three digits; fill the gaps with zeros.

misconceptions.ask: Which part did you hear second, and which box is it for?
misconceptions.repair: Thousands go in the middle box and the ones part at the end, whatever their size.

listen_for: write them next to each other
misconceptions.ask: How many digits does a number in the millions have?
misconceptions.repair: A number in the millions has seven digits; the parts go into the boxes, not after each other.

misconceptions.ask: Where do we start counting three digits for a comma?
misconceptions.repair: Commas are put from the ones end: three digits, comma, three digits, comma.

checks.question: Write 7 million, 30 thousand and 450 in symbols.
Write two million, five hundred and six thousand and twelve in figures.

skills.key_step: The child splits the number at the comma, reads the thousands part and then the last three digits, and says nothing for a zero.

floor.prerequisite: Reads and writes numbers up to 10,000 in words.
floor.question: Write 4,506 in words.
floor.answer: four thousand, five hundred and six

representations: the number split at the comma into two parts
each part read as a small number with its name
a cheque or receipt with the amount in words
steps: Split the number at the comma.
Read the first part and say "thousand".
Read the last three digits as hundreds, tens and ones.
Use "and" before the tens or ones and a hyphen for twenty-one to ninety-nine.
contexts: writing a cheque for school fees
a radio announcement of a crowd
the number of bags of maize at a depot

board.do: Write 45,320 and draw a line at the comma.
Point at the 45.
board.say: How do we read this part?

board.do: Wait for "forty-five thousand".
Point at 320.
Ask the child to write the whole number in words before you do.

misconceptions.ask: What does the 3 stand for?
misconceptions.repair: Read all three digits after the comma: three hundred and twenty.

misconceptions.ask: Say fourteen and forty slowly. Which one ends in a zero?
misconceptions.repair: Teen numbers end with the digit; -ty numbers end with a zero.

misconceptions.ask: Do we say zero when we read 506?
misconceptions.repair: A zero is an empty place and is not said.

misconceptions.ask: How many digits does a number in the tens of thousands have?
misconceptions.repair: Use five place boxes: sixty thousand fills the first two, the 5 goes in the ones.

checks.question: Write 70,409 in words.
checks.answer: seventy thousand, four hundred and nine

checks.question: Write "eighty-three thousand and fifteen" in figures.
checks.shows: words to figures with a zero

skills.key_step: The child counts the digits first, and when the counts are the same compares place by place from the left, stopping at the first difference.
representations: numbers written one under the other, lined up on the right
a place value chart with the first different place shaded
a number line with the numbers marked
steps: Count the digits: more digits is bigger.
Line the numbers up on the right.
Compare from the left and stop at the first place that differs.
Write the order the question asks for, and use < or > with the open end to the bigger number.
contexts: crowds at three stadiums
prices of second-hand cars
the number of learners in sub-counties

board.do: Write 62,815 and 62,951 one under the other.
Point at the ten thousands and the thousands.
Point at the hundreds.
Wait for the child to say which number is larger and why.

misconceptions.ask: How many digits does each number have?
misconceptions.repair: Count the digits first: a five-digit number is bigger than any four-digit number.

misconceptions.ask: Read the question again: smallest first or largest first?
misconceptions.repair: Underline the direction word before you start.

listen_for: the arrow points to the big one
misconceptions.ask: Which side of > is open wide?
misconceptions.repair: The open end faces the bigger number.

listen_for: it ends in a bigger number
misconceptions.ask: Which is the first place, from the left, where they are different?
misconceptions.repair: Stop at the first place that differs from the left; the ones come last.

checks.question: Order from smallest to largest: 58,302; 9,980; 58,230; 60,001
checks.shows: digit count then place by place

skills.key_step: The child finds the two thousands the number lies between and looks only at the hundreds digit to decide which is nearer.
representations: a number line between two thousands with the halfway mark
the number with the thousands digit circled and the hundreds digit underlined
a newspaper figure for a crowd
steps: Circle the thousands digit.
Look at the hundreds digit only.
5 or more: add one thousand; less than 5: keep the thousands.
Write zeros in the hundreds, tens and ones.
contexts: a newspaper rounding a crowd
the population of a town
the price of a dairy cow

board.do: Draw a number line from 67,000 to 68,000 with 67,500 in the middle.
Point at the halfway mark.
board.say: Is 67,449 before or after the middle?

board.do: Wait for the child to place 67,449.
Mark 67,449 just before the middle and write 67,000.

misconceptions.repair: Look at the hundreds digit: 5 or more rounds up.

misconceptions.ask: Which digit is just to the right of the thousands digit?
misconceptions.repair: Only the hundreds digit decides when rounding to the nearest thousand.

misconceptions.ask: Is 39 about the same size as 38,700?
misconceptions.repair: Write the zeros: the rounded number is 39,000.

misconceptions.ask: Which two thousands is 49,600 between?
misconceptions.repair: Rounding 49 thousands up gives 50 thousands.

listen_for: first the tens then the hundreds
misconceptions.ask: Which digit tells us, and what is it?
misconceptions.repair: Look at the hundreds digit once; do not round the other digits first.

checks.question: Round 67,449 to the nearest thousand.
checks.shows: one look at the hundreds digit

skills.key_step: The child says that squaring means the number times itself and shows it as a square of rows and columns.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the multiplication facts to 12 x 12.
floor.question: What is 9 x 9?

representations: a square of dots (9 rows of 9)
a square plot drawn on squared paper
the number times itself written as a multiplication
steps: Read the small 2 as "times itself".
Write the multiplication: 23 x 23.
For a multiple of ten, multiply the digits and write both zeros: 3 tens x 3 tens = 9 hundreds.
Check the answer lies between the squares of the tens on either side.
contexts: a square shamba
chairs set in a square for a parade
tiles on a square floor

board.do: Draw a 9 by 9 square of dots.
Count one row and the number of rows with the child.
Point at the whole square.
Wait for the child to say 81.
Write 9 squared = 9 x 9 = 81.

misconceptions.ask: Draw 9 squared as dots: how many rows, and how many in each row?
misconceptions.repair: The small 2 means the number times itself, not times 2.

misconceptions.ask: What is 3 tens times 3 tens?
misconceptions.repair: 30 x 30 is 9 hundreds, 900: both zeros are kept.

misconceptions.ask: Is 23 x 23 more than 20 x 20?
misconceptions.repair: Square the whole number, not each digit.

misconceptions.ask: Draw 21 by 21 as 20 + 1 each way. Which pieces did you leave out?
misconceptions.repair: There are also two strips of 20 x 1, so 21 squared is 400 + 20 + 20 + 1.

skills.key_step: The child asks which number times itself gives the square and checks the root by squaring it.
representations: a square plot with its area written inside
a list of squares to search
the root checked by multiplying back
steps: Ask: which number times itself gives this?
For a number ending in two zeros, take the root of the front and write one zero.
Try a number and square it.
If no whole number works, say it is not a perfect square.
contexts: the side of a square plot
a square classroom floor
a square parade of learners

board.do: Draw a square plot and write 144 m2 inside it.
Point at one side.
Wait for the child to try a number.
Write the child's number times itself and work it out together.

misconceptions.ask: What is 32 x 32?
misconceptions.repair: The square root times itself gives the number; half does not.

misconceptions.ask: What is 90 x 90?
misconceptions.repair: Two zeros in the square become one zero in the root: the root of 900 is 30.

misconceptions.ask: What is 7 x 7?
misconceptions.repair: If squaring the root does not give the number exactly, it is not a perfect square.

misconceptions.ask: Is 144 the distance round the plot or the space inside it?
misconceptions.repair: Area is side times side, so find the number that times itself gives 144.

checks.question: What is the square root of 6,400?
